ai.title: ‘AMERICA GETS SCREWED’, SCHUMER Accuses Trump & Lutnick of Selling US National Security to China
ai.description: WASHINGTON — U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer delivered a sharp rebuke of President Donald Trump’s administration on the Senate floor, accusing the White House and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick of compromising U.S. national security by approving the export of more than 800,000 advanced artificial intelligence chips to Chinese firms, including entities linked to China’s People’s Liberation Army. Addressing lawmakers in Washington, D.C., Schumer urged Congress to pass the AI Overwatch Act, the Match Act, and the Chip Security Act to curb technology transfers to Beijing. The New York Democrat also criticized the administration’s handling of recent widespread U.S. technology outages following the dismissal of National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross, calling on President Trump and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to assemble an intelligence red team to investigate the disruptions by December 1. Additionally, Schumer highlighted foreign lobbying allegations involving former White House communications director Jason Miller, vowing that the incoming Democratic congressional majority will prioritize aggressive oversight and anti-corruption reforms.
